It is Meccan, and its verses number seventeen.

Al-Nasa'i narrated from Jabir, who said: "Mu'adh prayed the Maghrib and recited al-Baqarah or al-Nisa'. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: Are you causing trouble, O Mu'adh? Would it not have sufficed you to recite 'By the sky and the Tariq,' and 'By the sun and its brightness,' and the like of these?"

[1–4] "By the sky and the Tariq. And what will make you know what the Tariq is? It is the piercing star. There is no soul but that it has over it a guardian."

"By the sky and the Tariq. And what will make you know what the Tariq is? The piercing star." Then in the usage of the language it became a name for one who walks the road, on the notion that he strikes it with his foot, and it became so well known in this sense that it became a literal meaning. The naming of one who comes at night as "tariq" is because he usually finds the doors closed and so knocks upon them.

The definite article in "al-najm" (the star) is generic. The root meaning of "al-thuqb" (piercing) is breaking through; so "al-thaqib" is the one who breaks through, and then it came to mean the shining one, on the notion that it pierces the darkness or the heavens. Its being left vague and then explained carries a glorification of its status and an alert to reflection and inference from it.

"Ma" is a supplementary particle, and the "lam" is the distinguishing one. It has also been read "lamma" with the doubled form, on the basis that it means "illa" (except), the exceptive, and "in" is a negation, and the predicate is omitted, i.e.: no soul exists in any state of the states except in the state that over it there is a guardian and watcher; and "kull" in this reading is emphatic, because "nafs" in that case is indefinite in the context of negation, so it generalizes.

Ibn Jarir said: The reading I choose over any other is the light form, because that is the well-known speech of the Arabs. Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 86, verses 5–10:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[5–10] ﴿So let man look at what he was created from. He was created from a gushing fluid, emerging from between the backbone and the ribs.﴾ ﴿Indeed, He is Able to return him.﴾ ﴿On the Day when secrets are scrutinized.﴾ ﴿Then he will have no power nor any helper.﴾

(p-6123) ﴿So let man look at what he was created from﴾ ﴿He was created from a gushing fluid﴾ [al-Tariq: 6] is the answer to an implied condition. The fa' is fasihah (an eloquent connective), meaning: if a doubter doubts that over every soul there is a watcher, then let him look, etc.

Al-Imam said: His words ﴿So let man look﴾ serve as evidence for the claim sworn to, as an additional emphasis. The reason is that the gushing fluid is a liquid in which there is no shaping or proportioning of the instruments through which the effect of life appears, such as the organs and the like. Then this fluid develops into a complete creature like a human being, filled with life, intellect and perception, capable of carrying out the vicegerency on earth. This shaping, proportioning, the creation of the bodily organs and instruments, the deposit in each organ of the power by which it can perform its function in the body, and then the granting of the power of perception and intellect, all of this cannot be without a guardian who watches over it all and manages it, and He is God, majestic is His glory. It is also possible that His words ﴿So let man look at what he was created from﴾ are a branch built upon what was established in the first matter, as if He says: since you know that over every soul there is a watcher, it is obligatory upon man not to neglect himself, and to reflect on his creation and how the beginning of his formation occurred, so that through this he arrives at the realization that He who originated him the first time is able to restore him; thus he takes himself to righteous deeds and good conduct, and turns it away from the paths of evil, for the eye of the watcher never ceases to be upon it in any state. End.

And ﴿dafiq﴾ [al-Tariq: 6] is from al-daf', which is pouring with force in it. It has been said that it means madfuq (poured), and that the active participle is used in the sense of the passive, just as the passive can be used in the sense of the active, as in: ﴿a veil that is screened﴾ [al-Isra: 45].

The correct view is that it carries the sense of the relative (nisbah), like laban and tamir, meaning: possessor of gushing, which applies to both the agent and the object. Or it is a metaphor in the attribution, where what belongs to its owner is attributed to the fluid for emphasis. Or it is an implicit or explicit metaphor in making it gushing, because of the succession of its drops, as if one drop pushes another, i.e., drives it. Or dafiq means poured out without any interpretation, as reported from al-Layth. These are opinions.

And His words, exalted is He: ﴿emerging from between the backbone and the ribs﴾ [al-Tariq: 7], meaning: from between the backbone of the man and the chest of the woman.

(p-6124) Al-Imam said: al-Sulb is every bone of the back that contains vertebrae, and it is expressed in common speech as the spine. It may also be used in the sense of the back itself, using the name of the part for the whole. "Al-tara'ib" is the place of the necklace on the chest, and by al-sulb he refers to the man, and by al-tara'ib to the woman. That is, that gushing fluid becomes the material for the creation of the human only when it issues from between the man and the woman and falls into the place where God's custom is to create it, which is the womb of the woman. So His words "emerging" etc. are a description that must be mentioned to explain that man is created only from gushing fluid that fulfills the conditions for the validity of creation from it.

Some scholars of medicine said: al-tara'ib is the plural of tariba, which is the bones of the chest in both male and female, and its usage is most common for the place of the necklace in the female. From it is the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

"Her ribs are polished like a mirror."

He said: The meaning of the verse is that the semen, with respect to its origin which is blood, emerges from something extended between the backbone, i.e., the vertebrae of the spine in the man, and the ribs, i.e., the bones of his chest. That extended thing between them is the aorta (al-Awrutiyy), which is the largest artery in the body, emerging from the heart behind the ribs and extending nearly to the end of the backbone. From it emerge a number of great arteries, among them two long arteries that emerge from it (p-6125) after the two renal arteries, and descend to the lower abdomen until they reach the two testicles, or the two spermatic arteries. Therefore He, exalted, says of the semen ﴿emerging from between the backbone and the ribs﴾ [al-Tariq: 7], because it emerges from a place between them, which is the aorta or the abdominal aorta. On this interpretation this verse is counted among the scientific miracles of the Qur'an, and this view is more apt and more precise than the first interpretation. End.

And His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He﴾ [al-Tariq: 8], i.e., the Guardian, glorified is He, mentioned in His words: ﴿over every soul there is a watcher﴾ [al-Tariq: 4], or the Creator understood from "was created." ﴿Is Able to return him﴾ [al-Tariq: 8], i.e., the return of man and his restoration in the second creation, is indeed able, as He was able to originate him in the first creation.

﴿On the Day when secrets are scrutinized﴾ [al-Tariq: 9], i.e., they will become manifest, and the hidden contents of hearts will be known.

Al-Zamakhshari said: al-sara'ir are what is concealed in the hearts of beliefs and intentions and other things, and what is hidden of deeds. Its bala' (scrutiny) is to know and examine it, and to distinguish between what was good in it and what was corrupt.

﴿Then he will have no power nor any helper﴾ [al-Tariq: 10], i.e., no power by which he could ward off the punishment of God and His painful retribution, and no helper who would support him and rescue him from whoever has inflicted harm upon him. The meaning is that he has lost what he was accustomed to in this world, when he used to rely on strength within himself or on his clan, by which he would ward off those who intended him harm. A helper is an ally who supports him against one who wronged and oppressed him. Nothing remains for him except awaiting the recompense for what he has sent forward.
